item.title: PowerCut 0.7.6
item.description:
• Auto Detect for mixed-language clips, in beta: Whisper re-detects the spoken language about every 30 seconds and writes each part in its own script. One clip, several languages, one transcript. Find it at the bottom of every language menu.
  • One export dialog for transcripts and captions: choose the full record, cuts struck through, or the video edit only, then deliver it in the original languages or translated to English. The translation happens at export time; your project and edit are never changed, strikes map onto the English words by time, and results are cached so repeat exports are instant.
  • English captions for foreign-language edits: the same language choice applies to the .srt export, so a Hindi edit ships with English captions in one step.
  • The export dialog calls out clips that have no transcript yet instead of leaving them silently missing.

item.title: PowerCut 0.7.5
item.description:
• Translate to English, in beta: Whisper listens to the spoken language and writes the transcript in English, every word timed to the original footage, so cuts land exactly where things were said. Per clip from any language menu, or the whole project from the Translate button. Pick the language or let Auto Detect handle it.
  • Your edit survives translation: strikes and cuts stay where they are in the footage, mapped by time onto the English words, or run the Auto Edit Pass fresh. Nothing is touched until the translation actually succeeds, so a failed download or an offline moment loses nothing.
  • New Transcription Accuracy setting: Standard, or Maximum with OpenAI's full Large-v3 model, noticeably more accurate on Hindi and translation (about a 3 GB one-time download). In Settings, the settings column, and the Translate dialog.
  • English scripts now guide take picking on translated footage, and Hinglish is available as a translation source.
  • Sturdier transcription pipeline ordering and more robust undo around in-flight background work.

item.title: PowerCut 0.7.4
item.description:
• New Document view: your transcript as a clean paper page. Serif type, margin timestamps, clip headings, whole-document zoom. Read-only preview by default with click-to-play on every word; press Edit Document for full editing: strike, restore, correct, and move material right on the page.
  • A follow-along cursor tracks the playhead word by word while the video plays, and the page scrolls with it. Clicking a clip in the footage column jumps the document to that section.
  • See the cut your way: Strike Thru Cuts shows the full transcript with cut material struck through, plain text with it off, or Hide Cuts for a clean read. With the full transcript showing, playback switches to full footage so every line plays, cut or kept.
  • Word document export in three flavors: the full uncut record, the edited transcript with real strikethrough, or only what made the video edit. Also in the File menu with XML and caption export.
  • Footage column: select several clips with Cmd or Shift click and remove them together; one undo brings them all back.
  • Faster document scrolling on long projects, button labels that survive smaller windows, a tinted highlight on moved material, and safer Word export that never overwrites a file until the new one is complete.

item.title: PowerCut 0.7.3
item.description:
• Two more languages, in beta: Hindi and Hinglish, carried by a new on-device Whisper engine. Thirteen languages total. The Whisper model downloads once on first use (about 1.5 GB) and everything stays on your Mac.
  • Fixed a freeze when importing very large batches of clips at once. Drop in 44 clips; they now flow through in seconds instead of hanging the app.
  • Devanagari sentence marks (danda) are understood by the pacing engine.

item.title: PowerCut 0.7.2
item.description:
• Try styles without losing work: switching Video Style saves your current edit to Versions first and asks what you want, re-tune the timing only, or also re-run the Auto Edit Pass for the new feel. Come back to a style you edited under before and PowerCut offers that edit back, exactly as you left it.
  • Every video style now explains itself: a caption under the picker describes what the selected style does to pacing and pauses.

item.title: PowerCut 0.7.1
item.description:
• Five more languages, in beta: Japanese with the full pipeline (filler and stutter detection included), plus Korean, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional) and Cantonese with transcription, pause cuts and the whole paper edit. Pick per project or per clip; each clip card now has a language dropdown.
  • Hide Cuts (formerly Struck) now gives a truly clean read: struck text collapses behind faint marks, fully struck passages fold into a single line, and the timeline switches to the edited view. The timeline's own Hide Cuts toggle stays independent.
  • Stray single-word edits between cuts (a marooned "So" making a half-second clip) are struck automatically. Restorable like every automatic strike, and it learns from your restores.
  • Tooltips across the whole interface, and a crash fix when hiding struck text.

item.title: PowerCut 0.7.0
item.description:
• Six languages: transcribe projects in English, Spanish, French, German, Italian or Portuguese. Pick the main language on the start page, or set a language per clip from the sidebar. Models download once, on first use.
  • Transcript scrolling is dramatically smoother on long projects.
  • Exports are frame-exact: adjacent cuts tile precisely, with no one-frame drift.
  • Multi-track audio extraction streams to disk, so very long recordings no longer spike memory.
  • Switching a clip's audio track or language mid-analysis can no longer mix results from the old run.

item.title: PowerCut 0.6.2
item.description:
• Find in transcript (⌘F): search every clip for words or phrases, close matches included, with a results list showing timecode, clip and match percentage. Matches highlight in the transcript.
  • Corrections at scale: fix a mis-heard word everywhere in the project in one step, and optionally remember it for every future transcript. Every automatic correction now shows a teal underline with what was heard, and right-click reverts it.
  • Keyboard fixes: typing in any text field never triggers shortcuts, S now strikes or restores in one key, and word corrections have a Cancel button.
  • Window resizing is smooth, and PowerCut wears its new icon.

item.title: PowerCut 0.6.1
item.description:
• Missing footage is now handled the way an editor would want. If a drive is unplugged or a file moves, the clip stays in your project marked in red, with the transcript and every edit intact. Playback holds its place, and you keep editing from the saved data.
  • Exports still include offline clips, referencing the original files, so Final Cut, Resolve and Premiere show them as offline media and relink the moment the files are back.
  • Plug the drive back in and everything heals automatically. Files that moved: right-click the clip and choose Locate Missing File.

item.title: PowerCut 0.6.0
item.description:
• MXF import. Sony, Canon and Panasonic broadcast files drop straight into PowerCut: transcribe, edit and export like any other clip. Camera timecode and every audio track come along.
  • Exports still reference your original MXF files, untouched, so Final Cut, Resolve and Premiere relink to the camera originals.
  • Powered by a bundled FFmpeg helper (LGPL) that repackages MXF losslessly where macOS allows, with a fast preview fallback where it doesn't. Audio is always untouched.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.10
item.description: • Fixes a crash at launch when the last project's footage can't be found (for example, an unplugged external drive). PowerCut now opens normally and lists the missing files instead.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.9
item.description:
• Recent Projects in the File menu: your last ten projects, one click to reopen. The current edit always autosaves before switching.
  • Projects without a name now autosave as Untitled_01, Untitled_02 and so on, and follow along when you give them a real name. No more hunting for an edit you forgot to name.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.8
item.description:
• Camera timecode handled per camera and per NLE: DJI (and any camera writing a real timecode track) lines up at source timecode in Final Cut, Resolve and Premiere.
  • Sony footage exports import cleanly into Final Cut Pro again (no more "invalid edit" warnings), while Resolve keeps the timecode form it needs to link Sony files.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.7
item.description:
• Clips in the sidebar can be dragged to reorder again: the card lifts, the others move apart as you go, and one Undo covers the whole move.
  • The clip count now reads "2 of 5 on" when some clips are switched off.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.6
item.description:
• After the free trial, PowerCut now stays fully usable: editing, transcription and the auto pass all keep working, and only export needs a license. The trial-end screen no longer locks the whole app.
  • Enter License sits right beside Unlock, so a purchased key is never a hunt.
  • Add Footage moved to the top of the sidebar, under the project name.
  • Named projects export to Final Cut Pro with the event and timeline under exactly that name.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.5
item.description:
• Final Cut Pro import fixed for Sony camera footage: multicam exports no longer trigger "Invalid edit with no respective media." Resolve exports keep their timecode-based form.
  • Timeline trimming is now frame-accurate, like trimming in Final Cut Pro: the edge stays exactly where you release it instead of snapping back.
  • Transcript words strike or restore only when the trim covers or reveals the whole word - shaving frames off a word edits the audio without changing the text.
  • Dragging a trim out and back in now behaves chronologically: the latest drag always wins.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.4
item.description:
• Sony camera timecode is now written into Final Cut and Resolve exports, so DaVinci Resolve links FX3 and other Sony MP4 clips correctly.
  • Cut padding now applies to every cut, including removed takes and filler words, and the sliders update the edit reliably.
  • Words at the end of a sentence are no longer clipped when the next take is removed.
  • Striking and restoring words is much faster, and rapid edits no longer stall playback.
  • Reset buttons on the Pauses and Cut Padding panels.
  • Footage Brief highlights clear when you click elsewhere, and the auto pass shows its progress while it runs.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.3
item.description:
PowerCut 0.5.3

  • Final Cut Pro imports without warnings. Exports now carry the format names Final Cut expects, so it no longer reports an unexpected value on the timeline or on multicam clips.
  • Better timeline size. The project is built on a standard Final Cut format chosen from the footage the cut is actually made of, rather than inheriting an odd capture size from whichever clip happened to be first. A screen recording in your story no longer sets the resolution for the whole project.
  • Multicam exports import cleanly, following on from the multicam fix in 0.5.2.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.2
item.description:
PowerCut 0.5.2

  • Final Cut Pro multicam export fixed. The multicam option wrote a file Final Cut rejected without an error, so nothing appeared on import.
  • Cuts land where they should. Edit points are now found in the audio itself rather than from transcript timings, so clips start right before the first word and end after the last one finishes, with no chopped words and no dead air at the head.
  • Breaths and long pauses removed between sentences, with the padding sliders genuinely controlling how the edit breathes.
  • Much stronger repeat and false start detection: re-read lines are matched against your script, restarts buried inside a sentence are caught, and mis-transcribed repeats no longer slip through.
  • Run Auto Edit Pass now re-derives cleanly instead of layering on the previous pass, so improved detection applies to projects you already started.
  • Click a word to play from it. Clicking selects the word and starts playback at that moment.
  • New Project in the File menu, and Previous Projects on the name pill.
  • Smoother settings sliders with a confirmation before re-planning, a larger selection popup, and panels that stay usable at small window sizes.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.1
item.description:
PowerCut 0.5.1

  • New transcript click model: click places the caret, double-click selects a word, triple-click selects a paragraph. Delete toggles strike and restore.
  • Playback speeds now go to 2x, with a compact speed menu next to the timeline play button.
  • Previous Projects dropdown on the project name pill, listing your five most recent projects.
  • Granular audio selection: pick the left or right channel of any track for transcription, right from the clip's context menu.
  • Larger default transcript text with a numeric size indicator.
  • Hover a clip to remove it, a visible audio track chip, and an optional auto-transcribe on import setting.
  • Many smaller fixes from tester feedback.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.0
item.description:
PowerCut 0.5.0

First test build: on-device transcription and rough cuts, paper editing, the Auto Edit Pass, take detection, the review queue, versions, and export to Final Cut Pro, DaVinci Resolve and Premiere Pro plus captions.
